name: Separate workforce-integrity and customer AML/PF control surfaces

attribution.legal_posture: Official jurisdiction-specific supervisory guidance. Customer-side laundering is framed as a possibility rather than an observed event; employee screening and customer AML determinations remain distinct.

caveats: Customer AML controls address customer transactions; employee indicators address workforce review and DPRK-linkage assessment; each question requires its own evidence.
Employee-risk and customer-AML processes address distinct populations and remain separate.
Legal and reporting obligations are jurisdiction-specific; this record supplies context rather than universal legal advice.

Nationality, language, appearance, geography, payment method, remote-work preference, device, network, and any single behavioral signal require independent corroboration before supporting DPRK linkage.
Prospective guidance, scenarios, and red flags describe controls and possibilities; incident or attribution status remains unassigned.
The customer-laundering scenario is presented as a possibility; the source frames gambling-operator use as a scenario rather than an observed DPRK IT-worker case.
The March 25, 2026 web page announces the attached report; both records remain prospective guidance rather than an observed gambling-sector incident.
Use proportionate, documented, privacy-preserving human review and jurisdiction-appropriate legal advice.

infrastructure.statement: The GSC treats the risk as two distinct control surfaces. For staff and contractors, it recommends identity and beneficiary continuity, remote-access restrictions, protection of proprietary and personal information, virtual-asset wage caution, and HR/staffing-firm training. For customers and virtual-asset activity, it directs operators to existing due diligence, source-of-funds, enhanced due diligence, transaction monitoring, blockchain-analysis, and financial-intelligence reporting controls. This is a useful architecture-level finding because it avoids treating applicant screening alone as sufficient.

sources.support: The report identifies remote staffing exposure for an IT-intensive sector and a separate possibility that customer-facing gambling or virtual-asset functions could be used for layering. It pairs staff-integrity controls with customer AML/PF controls and reporting duties. It does not claim a known gambling-sector incident. Evidence class: primary regulator guidance synthesizing official and attributed private-sector reporting; prospective for the regulated sector
